## Consensus Strengths

1. **The paper argues against itself harder than a referee would.** §2.3 withdraws
   its own "not forced" claim on discovering the readout is affine; §2.2 withdraws
   three successive framings of the no-diet gradient and names the one that
   survives; §2.2's residual-correction table shows six variants and reports that
   five of them destroy the no-diet result; §E2.1 records an earlier simulation
   that ran the nuisance backwards and inverted the artefact's sign. Supplementary
   Note S1 is a standing list of corrections to the authors' own analyses. This is
   not routine and it materially raises confidence in what survives.
2. **The negative results are bounded, not merely unrejected.** §2.6.2 does not stop
   at failing to find a shape-bias/human-agreement relationship: over 189 readouts
   (21 `w` × 9 runs) with `w` chosen post hoc per seed to maximise agreement, the
   best result never exceeds 20.7% of the human–human κ ceiling, and equivalence
   intervals fixed in advance (§77.5) exclude a κ change larger than 0.037 across a
   0.706 span of shape bias. A bounded null over an optimised readout family is
   much stronger evidence than a two-model comparison.
3. **The instrument is validated in both directions before it is trusted.** The
   ventral-gradient estimator is checked against a manufactured-zero condition
   (artefact is positive and rising where the effect is negative and falling —
   wrong sign twice) and a known-gradient recovery condition (ρ = +1.000 in 8/8 on
   both arms). §2.6.2 supplies a positive control for the error-consistency
   measure: the same machinery on the same images recovers 24.1% of ceiling on
   image difficulty against 8.7% on the shape/texture decision, so a flat decision
   result is not a dead instrument.
4. **The architectural control is an algebraic identity, not a statistical one.**
   `TwoStreamNetwork` initialises both trunks bit-identically (0 of 120 tensor
   pairs differ) and the `rgb_tsn` control returns a stream difference of exactly
   +0.0000 after 150 epochs. Every stream difference in the paper is therefore
   attributable to input by construction.

## Consensus Weaknesses

1. **[§2.3, §4.3] The central mechanism is an identity of the readout the authors
   chose, and no nonlinear readout is tested.** The classifier is
   `AdaptiveAvgPool2d → Flatten → Linear` and the fusion weights sum to one, so
   `clf(w·y₁+(1−w)·y₂) = w·clf(y₁)+(1−w)·clf(y₂)` holds to 1.1 × 10⁻⁶. The paper
   states this plainly and withdraws the "monotonicity was measured" claim — but
   the strong form of the title ("within this family the rate is a free parameter
   of the readout") is then a property of *affine* readouts. Real classifier heads
   are frequently nonlinear and any biological readout certainly is. The paper
   does not test whether the rate still spans the range, or whether monotonicity
   survives, under a nonlinear head over the same frozen features.
2. **[§2.2(b), §4.7] The load-bearing cortical result is one survivor of seven
   regional hypotheses at n = 8, and the design admits no multiplicity
   correction.** The authors disclose this unusually well — six failures are named
   — and correctly observe that the exact Wilcoxon floor (.0078125) cannot clear
   .05/m for any m > 6, so Holm and BH both return .141. But the paper's cortical
   claim still rests on a post-hoc-selected ROI contrast, and the controls offered
   (blur removal, monotonicity, cross-codebase replication, global-preference)
   address confounding rather than selection, as §2.2 itself says.
3. **[repository] Reproducibility falls below NMI's referee-availability standard.**
   `setup.cfg` `install_requires` carries no version pins at all (`torch`,
   `numpy`, `torchvision` unbounded); three dependencies are git URLs to lab
   repositories with no pinned commit (`lightning_kietzmannlab`, `neuroai`,
   `nsd_visuo_semantics`); **the `DVD` package that implements the paper's core
   front-end transform is commented out** of that list; `python_requires = >=3.8`
   contradicts the manuscript's stated Python 3.11.15; `README.md` is unmodified
   cookiecutter boilerplate for an upstream package (`pip install two_stream_dvd`,
   with KietzmannLab PyPI/codecov badges) and contains no path from a command to a
   number in the paper; there is no `requirements.txt`, `environment.yml`, lock
   file, or `Dockerfile`. The manuscript's *Software and code* statement does give
   exact versions for fourteen packages read from installed metadata — which is
   better than most submissions — but it is prose that the repository's own
   declared dependencies contradict. NMI requires code central to the claims to be
   available to referees *during review*; the statement promises release "on
   acceptance" with no specific justification for the delay.
4. **[§2.3, Limitation 16] The control that carries the split claim is not
   capacity-matched.** `dkl_bcs_single` has half the parameters of the two-stream
   model, and the 0.088 shape-bias advantage (0.655 vs 0.567) is attributed to the
   architectural split. The pre-registered `resnet34` matched arm has not been run
   (PLAN §72.6). The authors state the confound direction, which helps, but the
   claim "having two components to integrate is worth 0.088" is exactly the one
   the missing arm tests.
5. **[whole manuscript] ~10,560 words of main-text body against NMI's ~3,000–5,000,
   and 14 display items against a cap of 6–8, with withdrawn-claim archaeology
   inline in Results.** (Measured on Abstract→Discussion: 10,564 words excluding
   table rows, headings, source lines and block quotes; 11,578 raw. Display items
   are 9 tables — only one of them numbered — plus Figures 1–5.) §2.2 in particular interleaves
   the surviving result with the provenance history of superseded numbers, a
   tautology the authors caught in their own earlier check, and a six-variant
   sensitivity table. All of this belongs in Supplementary — where S1 already
   exists for exactly this purpose — and its presence in Results makes the
   surviving claim harder to locate than the corrections to it.
6. **[§3, Discussion] The transferable result is under-led for this readership.**
   The Discussion states that the diet is not a training recommendation and that
   "its interest is as a model of development." For NMI the portable contribution
   is the measurement critique: shape bias is a readout statistic, it does not
   identify a representation, and it does not track human decision structure. That
   is a result about how the field evaluates vision models and it should lead.

## Author Questions

1. Does the readout claim survive a nonlinear head? Re-running §2.3's sweep with a
   one-hidden-layer MLP fusion over the same cached frozen features would settle
   whether "the rate is a free parameter of the readout" is a fact about mixing
   readouts or about affine ones.
2. What does a permutation null over hierarchical-rank labels across the 20 Kastner
   ROIs return for the V1v→hV4 gradient? That is the one calibration that speaks
   to selection rather than confounding, and the exact-test floor cannot supply it.
3. Will the code, a pinned environment manifest, and the `DVD` front-end
   dependency at a fixed commit be available to referees at review rather than on
   acceptance? If any part must be withheld, what is the specific reason?
4. Two residual provenance gaps in §2.2 are disclosed but unexplained — the diet
   column (whose solve requires a subject-01 value outside all 48 observed cells)
   and the untrained control, which moved in the opposite direction. Can the diet
   column be regenerated from the current fits, or is it in the same
   deleted-data category as the no-diet column?
5. `parvo_highsf` seed 0 is dropped from the behavioural row for deciding 139/150
   images. Was that exclusion rule fixed before the count was seen?

## Code Reproducibility

- Repository provided: yes, at `911ba8a` (not public — see the separate note on
  the third-party remote).
- README adequate: **no** — upstream cookiecutter boilerplate.
- Pinned dependencies: **no** — unpinned, plus three unpinned git URLs.
- Core dependency present: **no** — `DVD` is commented out of `install_requires`.
- Seeds documented and used: **yes** — seeds 0/1/2 throughout, reported per cell.
- Configs version-controlled: **yes** — 49 sbatch scripts, 249 Python modules,
  named by path in §4.1–§4.7.
- LICENSE: **yes** (BSD-3, correctly attributed). DOI: **no**.
- Provenance tooling: **above standard** — `verify_new_claims.py` pins 28 numeric
  claims against their source files and currently returns no failures;
  `results/visualrois/*.json` stamps inputs with size and mtime.
- Estimated time to reproduce the headline result from the artefacts as they
  stand: **> 1 week** (install would fail first). With a pinned manifest and the
  cached features: **< 1 day** for §2.3 and §2.6.2, which are exact arithmetic on
  stored logits.

## Specific Improvement Suggestions (ranked, with feasibility)

1. **Nonlinear-readout sweep** (§2.3). One MLP head over cached frozen features,
   3 seeds. Answers the highest-value objection. ≈ 1 day, no trunk retraining.
2. **Pinned environment manifest + rewritten README + `DVD` at a fixed commit.**
   Turns a Major-revision trigger into a Pass. ≈ 1 day, no compute.
3. **Permutation null over ROI rank labels** (§2.2b). Selection-aware calibration
   for the load-bearing cortical claim. ≈ 1 day CPU.
4. **`resnet34` parameter-matched single-stream arm** (Limitation 16). Already
   pre-registered with a decision rule. 3 seeds × ~2 days GPU.
5. **Cut Results to ~5,000 words; move all withdrawn-claim archaeology to S1.**
   ≈ 3 days writing, no compute. Also fixes Clarity.
6. **Re-lead the Discussion on the measurement critique** for an ML readership.
   ≈ 1 day writing.

==========================================
## Comments to Authors
==========================================

### Summary of key messages

You argue that the apparent conflict between shape-biased human cue-conflict
behaviour and texture-like descriptions of ventral cortex dissolves once
behaviour is treated as a readout over components rather than a report of one
representation. In a two-stream network receiving approximations of the
magnocellular and parvocellular signals, the luminance stream ends shape-biased
and the chromatic stream texture-biased; the shape-biased component is supplied
by the input and the texture-biased one is built by learning; fitted to eight NSD
subjects it is the texture-biased stream whose unique variance carries the ventral
end of the hierarchy; and the mixed readout is shape-biased. You then show that
reweighting that readout moves shape bias across the range the field's models
occupy without either representation changing, and that three properties commonly
treated as travelling with shape bias — effective dimensionality,
out-of-distribution robustness, and trial-by-trial agreement with human observers
— do not.

### Major comments

1. **The readout result is an identity of the affine head you chose.** §4.3
   specifies `AdaptiveAvgPool2d → Flatten → Linear` and fusion weights summing to
   one; §2.3 verifies `clf(w·y₁+(1−w)·y₂) = w·clf(y₁)+(1−w)·clf(y₂)` to
   1.1 × 10⁻⁶ and correctly withdraws the claim that monotonicity was measured.
   What remains unaddressed is the scope this leaves the title. If the rate's
   free-parameter status follows from affineness, then the claim is about affine
   readouts, and neither a nonlinear network head nor a biological readout is
   covered. Please re-run the §2.3 sweep with at least one nonlinear fusion or
   head over the identical frozen features and report whether the span and the
   monotonicity survive. If they do, the central claim is considerably stronger
   than the paper currently establishes; if they do not, the title needs the
   qualifier.
2. **§2.2(b) is a selected result and the paper's controls do not speak to
   selection.** You say so yourself, which is to your credit. But the cortical leg
   is what distinguishes this work from the prior dissociation literature
   (Hermann et al. 2020; Islam et al. 2021), so it carries weight it cannot
   currently support alone. A permutation null over hierarchical-rank labels
   across the 20 Kastner ROIs would calibrate the V1v→hV4 gradient against the
   family it was drawn from. This is the analysis the exact-test floor cannot
   substitute for, and it should sit beside the family-size disclosure rather than
   replace it.
3. **Code central to the claims is not available to referees.** The *Code
   availability* statement defers release to acceptance. NMI's policy is that such
   code be available during review. Separately, the repository as it stands cannot
   be installed: `setup.cfg` pins nothing, three dependencies are unpinned git
   URLs, the `DVD` package implementing your front end is commented out of
   `install_requires`, `python_requires = >=3.8` contradicts the Python 3.11.15 in
   your *Software and code* statement, and `README.md` is unmodified template text
   for an upstream package. Your manuscript-level version reporting is unusually
   thorough; please make the repository match it, and add a path from one command
   to one number that appears in a main-text table.
4. **The single-stream control is not capacity-matched** (Limitation 16). §2.3
   concludes that "having two components to integrate is still worth 0.088 over
   having one", against a control with half the parameters. You have
   pre-registered the `resnet34` arm with a decision rule; please run it, and if
   `resnet34`-single still exceeds 0.6749, restate §2.3's conclusion accordingly.
5. **Main text length and the placement of your own corrections.** At ~10,560
   body words the main text runs roughly 2–3× NMI's guidance, and it carries 14
   display items against a cap of 6–8, and much of §2.2's length is
   the history of superseded numbers, an earlier tautological check, and a
   six-variant sensitivity table. The transparency is valuable and should be kept
   — in Supplementary Note S1, which already exists for it. As written, a reader
   meets the corrections before the surviving claim.
6. **Consider what an ML readership takes away.** Your Discussion says the diet is
   not a training recommendation and that its interest is developmental. The
   result that transfers to this readership is the measurement one: a
   shape-bias rate does not identify a representation, and across 189 readouts of
   frozen components with `w` optimised post hoc it never reaches 21% of the
   human–human error-consistency ceiling. Leading with that would not change any
   claim; it would change which claim is first.

### Minor comments

- m1. §2.1 Table 1's untrained references are single models with no training seed,
  noted in footnote ᵇ. Consider moving that caveat into the row labels.
- m2. §2.4 excludes `parvo_highsf` seed 0 from the behavioural row for deciding
  139/150 images. State whether the threshold was fixed before the count was seen.
- m3. §2.7 reports that two of four front-end controls are degenerate on the
  cortical instrument (Uₚ = 0.006, Uₘ = 0.007). This bounds §2.2(b)'s control
  claim and should appear where the controls are first invoked, not only in §2.7.
- m4. §2.6.2's crossed cells resolve to neither cue on 70–85% of images against
  49–63% for matched cells; put those rates in the table rather than the prose.
- m5. §2.2's parenthetical that a pooled intercept "reports 42% and 0% and so
  understates this" will read as special pleading unless the pooled figure is
  shown alongside the per-ROI one.
- m6. `results/figures/` holds seven figures; the manuscript carries one
  figure/table caption inline. Confirm the display items and captions are
  assembled before submission.

### Notes by criterion

**Technical soundness.** The strongest axis. Bit-identical trunk initialisation
makes stream differences attributable to input by construction; the
manufactured-zero and known-gradient simulations bracket the encoding estimator
from both sides; the konio arm's magno-cancellation gate passed bit-exact; the
two-statistics rule is applied against the authors' interest more than once.

**Support for conclusions.** Generally strong, with two exceptions named above:
the readout claim over-reaches its affine demonstration, and the cortical claim
is selection-exposed. The paper's own scope statements are unusually accurate
about both.

**Significance and originality.** The dissociation between representational shape
content and behavioural rate is not new (Hermann et al. 2020; Islam et al. 2021),
and the manuscript says so explicitly rather than claiming priority. What is new
is the form: a fixed pair of representations with an exactly interpolating
readout, plus a cortical leg the prior work lacks, plus a bounded null on human
decision agreement. The bounded null is, to this referee, the most valuable
single contribution.

**Methodology and statistics.** Exact tests with their floors stated; no
multiplicity-corrected significance claimed anywhere, with an explicit argument
for why none is available at n = 8. This is the right call and it is argued, not
asserted. The consequence — that no single claim carries corrected significance
— should be visible in the Abstract, not only in §4.7.

**Reproducibility.** Manuscript-level version reporting is above standard; the
repository does not match it and cannot currently be installed. See major
comment 3.

**Clarity and presentation.** Dense, long, and organised around the authors'
epistemic history rather than the reader's path through the argument. See major
comment 5.

**Responsible AI and dual use.** No dual-use concern: no released model, no
deployment claim, no scraped or sensitive data. Ethics, consent and
constraints-on-generality are handled specifically rather than by boilerplate,
and the sex-as-a-biological-variable statement correctly distinguishes what is
unavailable per release rather than deferring in one sentence. Missing: total
training compute and any energy figure for the twelve-plus training runs.

==========================================
## Confidential Comments to the Editor
==========================================

**Triage.** Send out. This is not a benchmark paper and not an application paper;
it is a rigorous negative result about a metric the vision-model community uses
constantly, with a cortical leg. It clears scope on the "overturns a widely-held
belief" and "responsible-AI / evaluation" routes rather than on a capability
advance.

**Significance.** Would the field cite this in a year? Probably yes, but for the
measurement result rather than the model. Shape bias on the Geirhos set is one of
the most-used human-alignment numbers for vision models; a demonstration that it
is a free parameter of the readout over frozen representations, plus a bounded
null showing it does not track trial-level human agreement over an optimised
readout family, is directly consequential for how alignment claims are made. The
developmental-diet framing is the weaker half for this readership and the authors
themselves disclaim any training recommendation.

**Recommendation.** Major revision. Three of the six major comments are cheap to
satisfy (nonlinear readout over cached features; repository manifest; permutation
null), one is a known pre-registered training run, and two are writing. None
requires new data collection. The science that survives is unusually well
audited; the gap is between what the paper establishes and what its strongest
sentences claim, plus a repository that does not match its own methods section.

**Transfer.** Not needed at this stage. If the editors judge the ML-facing payoff
too thin after revision, Nature Communications is the natural alternative and
would not require the measurement critique to lead. I would not send this to a
domain neuroscience journal — the cortical leg is a selected n = 8 result and is
the paper's most exposed claim, whereas the readout and error-consistency results
are robust and are what a computational readership will use.

**Additional experiments, cost/benefit.** The nonlinear-readout sweep is the
highest ratio in the paper: about a day on cached features, and it either
strengthens the central claim materially or bounds it honestly. The permutation
null is comparable value for the cortical leg. The `resnet34` arm is worth it
because it is already pre-registered with a rule, so its outcome is
interpretable either way. I would not ask for more NSD subjects or more seeds:
the exact-test floor means additional subjects buy no inferential headroom, and
the authors are right that the design's evidence is separation and effect size
rather than p-values.

**Expertise and conflicts.** Confident on encoding models, variance
partitioning, cue-conflict methodology and reproducibility standards; less
expert on the developmental-vision literature the front end implements. No
conflicts.
